Bug_Title: Only one method invocation is expected when testing checked exceptions
Bug_Explanation: The code is attempting to check for an IOException using try-catch, but it calls both g() and f() in the same statement inside the try block. Therefore, it's unclear whether g() or f() is responsible for throwing the exception, violating the best practice of testing a single method invocation for exceptions.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug test case calls the showBug method of the ExceptionHandlingDemo class, which contains the bug at line 7. The showBug method attempts to call both g(f(1)) in a single statement, which can each throw an IOException. This violates the rule that only one method invocation is expected when testing checked exceptions, leading to ambiguity about which method caused the exception.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that the test passed successfully (OK (1 test)), showing no evidence of the bug being triggered during the test execution.
